featured_reviews.review_text: Sadicha Restaurant at MIG Club, Bandra serves a satisfying chicken thali with authentic homemade flavors. The curry is well-spiced, portions are filling, and service is quick. Simple ambiance, good value for money, and a comforting meal overall.

featured_reviews.name: Shyam Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: They have been serving delicious Maharashtrian food for over a decade now. It’s open only during lunch and dinner time. Prawns fry and Chicken sukha is a must try. Vegetarian options are as good as none.

featured_reviews.name: Manoj Arkar
featured_reviews.review_text: The food has no taste at all, how can you eat Malvani style food? A person should be satisfied after tasting the food. Their food is for show and the Solakdi should not be drunk. It tasted like water. The money was totally wasted.

featured_reviews.name: Ankita Mukul Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
Got to know about this place via Google as I was in BKC and wanted to eat fish, looking at the rating I thought of visiting this place.
The place is quite small and gives homely feeling, looking at this i got happy thinking the food would be really nice and homemade.
We ordered for a chicken thali, a pomfret thali and an surmai thali and a tisrya sukkah.
Was totally disappointed when the food came, the tisrya sukkha seemed like tisrya masala and was very sweet. The surmai thali was not upto the mark, surmai was very small, I have never had such small piece of surmai in any of the fish outlet.
Quantity wise I was totally disappointed, chicken thali had just 2 pieces of chicken.
Sol kadhi seemed to be like water added to it, we had reached around 2:30-2:45pm and I think we were served the left over food as it was closing time.
I will not recommend this restaurant to anyone, specially who is a fish lover.

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Amrute
featured_reviews.review_text:
In Mumbai, people are often misguided into thinking Mangalorean or Goan Cuisine as Malvani.. But not here…!!

So I came here today with a friend. He ordered a Tisrya (Clams) Thali and I called for Mori (Shark) Thali. Both were excellent. The fish was fresh and the gravy was very tasty and perfectly spiced. The quantity in each thali was perfect for one adult. If at all I have to complain then I would say, I missed the small portion of Suka Jawla (dry baby shrimp) that is also served as part of the seafood thali in my town.

The service was prompt and the staff was welcoming. Hygiene is taken care of. The place is tiny and very modestly done up, so if you value the ambience as much as your food, then this isn't the place for you. Free Street Parking is available.

If you are craving for good authentic Malvani Food… Sadichha is just the place for you.

featured_reviews.name: Deepthi Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find this place. It's located just opp the MIG club...it's a quaint tiny lil place..serving seafood like a boss! We ordered everything and lived everything. The bombil fry, prawns, mandeli, the pomfret stuffed with prawns (awesomeness) and all the thalis..we had prawn, mory, clams, surmai and pomfret thalis..and for vegetarians with us they specially made some pithala and a good veg thali :). Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: nirant palav
featured_reviews.review_text: It was a really great restaurant for sea food, Chicken Masala was so tasty, Mutton was well cooked and Bombil/Bombay Duck fry was an amazing must try dish if you visit the hotel, Do visit the Hotel for Just Bombil/Bombay Duck fry Really great taste and crispy

featured_reviews.name: S F
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was a favourite joint especially since our office was in bkc.
However my last visit was nothing short of a huge disappointment.
Menu has changed and even bombil is priced APS which is silly since bombil is not a premium fish . I paid 360 for a plate... Received burnt oily bombil... Not worth it.
The sol kadhi was watery, coconut milk seemed split.. no basic garnish of coriander and no taste of any spice..
Pics attached. This was a parcel pickup.
Avoid visiting.. these guys need to check what their chefs are doing.

featured_reviews.name: Nishad lad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very limited seating hence waiting time could be more. Service was good.
Food was very good and fresh. Bombil were delicious. Surmai thali, tandoor surmai thali was delicious. Prawns Koliwada was very good too. Chicken thali was delicious. Overall a great experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sanjana Bag
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Bombil fry was crispy and delicious, with three pieces served—quite satisfying. The Prawns Koliwada arrived hot and tasted really good. The Surmai tawa fry was just okay, nothing exceptional but decent.
The highlight was the Prawns Masala Thali. It is very cost-friendly and offers great value for money. The thali includes a good variety of items such as rice, three breads of your choice, prawns curry, papad, sukha machi, thecha, and sol kadi.

featured_reviews.name: Chanchal Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text: Tried the Mutton Thali, Chicken Malai Kebab, and Bombil Fish Fry—all absolutely worth it. Had to wait around 10 minutes, but the wait was totally justified. Service was quick, food came hot, and the seating is comfortable. Really liked how well they’ve managed the seating arrangement. Overall, a satisfying experience.

featured_reviews.name: Suvas Wagh
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a great place to have sea food in Mumbai. They have Multiple outlets in Mumbai. I visited this place with friends. Tried Surmai fry, Pomfret thali, Prawns thali, Prawns kolowada, Chicken lollipop and Chicken thali. We loved the food! All the fish served was very fresh and perfectly fried with amazing taste. Even the chicken tasted great. Also the quantity of food is good compared to cost, it can be improved. Service is also good. Might face waiting time of upto 15-20 mins on weekends.

But recommend to try their sea food.

featured_reviews.name: Masban Pereira
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of the best places for seafood lover’s especially the thali. My family and I have been her a number of time and this place doesn’t disappoint. Our favourites are the Surmai thali, shimpy thali, pomfret thali bombil thali and prawns thali. The portions size are decent and reasonably priced. You have options of bhakri, neer dosa or chapatis with the thali. We try and visit here at least once a month.

featured_reviews.name: Dipesh Malvade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Jaihind Lunch Home, Bandra today and it turned out to be a super satisfying food experience! 🤩🍽️✨
The restaurant gives a classic Mumbai dining vibe with a lively and welcoming atmosphere 🏙️🎶. Even though the place was quite busy, the service was quick, smooth and well managed 👏⚡
⭐ What I Ordered:
🍗 Chicken Lapeta Kebab – ₹390
Absolutely delicious! Perfectly grilled, juicy, smoky and nicely spicy 🌶️🔥. Every bite was full of flavour and cooked to perfection 🤤👌 Definitely a must-try if you love spicy starters!
🥘 Sukha Chicken Thali – ₹430
Authentic coastal style dish with rich and balanced flavours 🌴🍗. It felt like proper home-style Maharashtrian food 🏡❤️. Very filling, satisfying and full paisa vasool meal 😋
🥞 Neer Dosa (3 pcs) – ₹90
Soft, light, smooth and paired perfectly with the main dish 🧈🥥. Simple but very tasty and fresh ✨
🥥 Solkadhi – ₹90
Super refreshing, cool and perfectly balanced the spice level 🧊🥤🌸 Loved the taste and freshness!
💧 Mineral Water – ₹35
💰 Total Bill – ₹1087 💳🧾
Overall, the food quality, taste, portion size and service were really impressive ⭐👏. The place is perfect for family dining 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, friends outing 👫 and casual food plans 🍛🍹
If you are in Bandra and love authentic Maharashtrian & coastal food, you definitely need to visit 😉📍🍴

featured_reviews.name: vicky s
featured_reviews.review_text: I took surmai tawa thali. The surmai was fresh. The fish curry was yummy. Bhakri could have been better. Surmai, curry and rice together tasted heavenly. Must visit for fish lovers in BKC.

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

featured_reviews.name: Omshiv Pandey
featured_reviews.review_text:
Original Review Date: March 31, 2024
Date of Experience: January 20, 2024
Review Edited: October 2nd, 2025 (Reason: Original review was too honest that it did not comply with the Google's polices.)

Based on my three years of interaction with the Pukar Organization's year-long research program, I found the approach to self-development to be undermined by the organization’s overall environment.

My experience has been largely negative. During the introductory sessions, individuals were encouraged to express their personal values. However, if those views did not align with the organization's internal doctrines, staff and alumni often engaged in belittling behavior that made participants feel foolish and discouraged independent thought.

Despite operating as an NGO, Pukar Organization exhibited a clear, enforced bias, creating a culture where individuals were subtly pressured to comply with specific, predetermined worldviews. This went beyond educational guidance and felt like an attempt to indoctrinate Indian youth rather than fostering genuine, critical thinking.

This agenda was openly displayed at a Youth Day celebration for Alumni on January 20, 2024. During the event, staff and alumni actively diverted the focus to a polarizing public debate, using the platform to make highly derogatory and divisive comments toward widely held beliefs and cultural sentiments. This created an unprofessional and exclusionary atmosphere, further solidifying the sense that the NGO is prioritizing a personal agenda over its stated mission.

In conclusion, while every organization holds values, using an NGO platform to enforce personal, divisive agendas is unacceptable. I would refrain from being associated with this organization and urge others to be cautious when considering joining the Pukar Organization if you value an environment that genuinely supports diverse, independent thought.

featured_reviews.name: Prananjay Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahim Dargah Urus Ground is a significant and well-known gathering place associated with the annual Urs celebrations of Hazrat Makhdum Shah Baba at Mahim, Mumbai. The ground holds immense cultural, spiritual, and community importance, serving as a vibrant center where thousands of devotees and visitors come together to participate in one of the city's most respected religious events. It stands as a remarkable symbol of faith, unity, and tradition that has been cherished by generations.

One of the most admirable aspects of Mahim Dargah Urus Ground is the sense of togetherness it fosters among people from diverse backgrounds. During the Urs celebrations, the area becomes a beautiful example of communal harmony, where individuals from different communities gather with mutual respect and shared devotion. This spirit of inclusiveness reflects the timeless teachings of Sufism, which emphasize love, compassion, service, and brotherhood.

The atmosphere during the Urs celebrations is truly inspiring. The ground comes alive with devotional activities, cultural programs, and spiritual gatherings that create a unique and memorable experience for visitors.
